title: Rocky Mountain spotted fever: doxycycline inhibits protein synthesis
vignette: A previously healthy 24-year-old man is hospitalized due to 3 days of fever, chills, myalgia, and severe headache. The symptoms started on the last day of his camping trip in the Appalachian Mountains and have rapidly progressed. Temperature is 38.9 C (102 F), blood pressure is 100/56 mm Hg, and pulse is 120/min. On examination, the patient is lethargic and confused. There is no neck rigidity. The lungs are clear on auscultation and heart sounds are normal. The abdomen is soft and nontender. There is a prominent erythematous maculopapular rash on the distal forearms. No lymphadenopathy is present. The patient should be immediately initiated on a medication that targets which of the following?

clues.text: fever, chills, myalgia, and severe headache
clues.note: A nonspecific prodrome of fever, headache, and myalgia precedes the rash in Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF). Recognizing this early triad (before the rash fully develops) is what allows lifesaving empiric therapy.

clues.text: camping trip in the Appalachian Mountains
clues.note: Outdoor/tick exposure is the key risk factor. Despite the name, RMSF is concentrated in the eastern and south-central United States (e.g., the Appalachian and mid-Atlantic regions), transmitted by Dermacentor (dog/wood) ticks.

clues.text: erythematous maculopapular rash on the distal forearms
clues.note: A macular rash beginning peripherally (wrists/forearms and ankles) and spreading centripetally - and that can involve the palms and soles - is the classic RMSF pattern and the confirmatory clue here.

whatMatters: Tick/camping exposure + fever, headache, and myalgia + a maculopapular rash that starts on the wrists/forearms (peripheral, centripetal, can reach palms/soles) = Rocky Mountain spotted fever (Rickettsia rickettsii). Start empiric doxycycline immediately; it inhibits bacterial PROTEIN SYNTHESIS at the 30S ribosome. Answer C. Treat on suspicion - don't wait for serology.
strategy: Diagnose RMSF clinically (tick exposure + centripetal maculopapular rash), then map its drug (doxycycline) to its target = 30S ribosome -> protein synthesis. Match the distractors to their drug classes: DNA unwinding = fluoroquinolones (gyrase); folate = TMP-SMX; ergosterol = azoles (fungal); cell wall = penicillins (spirochetes); reverse transcription = antiretrovirals.

eliminations.label: Bacterial DNA unwinding - fluoroquinolones
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: fluoroquinolones inhibit DNA gyrase/topoisomerase II (DNA unwinding). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they are not first-line for RMSF, which requires doxycycline. ✅ Correct if: enteric fever/Salmonella or a gram-negative needing a quinolone.

eliminations.label: Bacterial folate metabolism - TMP-SMX
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sulfonamides/trimethoprim block folate synthesis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: sulfa drugs can actually WORSEN RMSF; the answer is doxycycline (protein synthesis), not folate. ✅ Correct if: PCP prophylaxis/treatment, UTI, or Nocardia.

eliminations.label: Fungal ergosterol synthesis - azoles
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: azoles inhibit fungal ergosterol synthesis (cell membrane). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: RMSF is bacterial, not fungal. ✅ Correct if: a fungal infection (e.g., histoplasmosis, candidiasis).

eliminations.label: Spirochetal cell wall formation - penicillin
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: penicillins block cell-wall (peptidoglycan) synthesis, used for spirochetes like Treponema. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: RMSF is a Rickettsia, not a spirochete; secondary syphilis also gives a palm/sole rash but with milder fever and lymphadenopathy. ✅ Correct if: secondary syphilis.

eliminations.label: Viral reverse transcription - antiretrovirals
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: NRTIs/NNRTIs block HIV reverse transcriptase. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: acute retroviral syndrome has a diffuse rash WITH lymphadenopathy, sore throat, and oral ulcers - and this patient has a tick exposure. ✅ Correct if: acute HIV (retroviral) syndrome.

reasoning: Tick habitat + fever/headache/myalgia + maculopapular rash on the wrists/forearms = Rocky Mountain spotted fever (Rickettsia rickettsii)
RMSF requires urgent empiric doxycycline (delay increases mortality)
Doxycycline binds the 30S ribosomal subunit and blocks aminoacyl-tRNA binding
-> inhibits bacterial protein synthesis; answer C
mechanism: RMSF is caused by Rickettsia rickettsii, an obligate intracellular, weakly gram-negative bacterium transmitted by Dermacentor (dog/wood) ticks in the eastern and south-central United States. It invades and lyses vascular endothelial cells, producing a small-vessel vasculitis manifesting as fever, headache, myalgia, and a maculopapular rash that classically begins on the wrists/ankles and spreads centripetally (often to the palms and soles), frequently with thrombocytopenia. First-line therapy is doxycycline, which binds the 30S bacterial ribosomal subunit and blocks binding of aminoacyl-tRNA, inhibiting protein synthesis; it must be started empirically on clinical suspicion because delayed treatment sharply increases mortality (even in children, doxycycline is preferred). The distractor targets correspond to fluoroquinolones (DNA gyrase), sulfonamides/trimethoprim (folate), azoles (ergosterol), penicillins (cell wall), and antiretrovirals (reverse transcriptase).

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid Micro > RMSF: R. rickettsii, Dermacentor tick, endothelial vasculitis, centripetal rash to palms/soles, thrombocytopenia; doxycycline (30S) started empirically; antimicrobial target map.

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: Two-step: identify RMSF, then map its drug (doxycycline) to its molecular target (protein synthesis, 30S).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on maculopapular, centripetal, obligate intracellular, 30S vs 50S, or vasculitis? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Each option is a different drug class's target. Doxycycline = protein synthesis (30S); quinolones = DNA gyrase; sulfa/TMP = folate; azoles = ergosterol; penicillin = cell wall; NRTIs = reverse transcriptase.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: tick + centripetal rash (palms/soles) = RMSF -> doxycycline (30S protein synthesis); treat first, test later.

keywords.front: Tick exposure + rash on wrists/ankles spreading inward (+/- palms/soles)

keywords.back: Blocks folate synthesis (dihydropteroate synthase + dihydrofolate reductase)

firstAid.detail: Micro: R. rickettsii, tick-borne; doxycycline (30S protein-synthesis inhibitor), start empirically.
firstAid.location: Micro: R. rickettsii, tick-borne; doxycycline (30S protein-synthesis inhibitor), start empirically.

firstAid.detail: Pharm > quinolones (gyrase), sulfa/TMP (folate), azoles (ergosterol), penicillins (cell wall), NRTIs (RT).

memoryHook: 'Rocky Mountain' but really the East Coast: tick + wrist-to-trunk rash = doxy, which jams the 30S protein line. Treat first, test later.
